title: Runtime hardening: agent-efficient responses, fail-closed guards, lifecycle optimization
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. This milestone hardens the bwrk runtime in three layers. Sprint H1 (free machinery): response-shape changes that derive from existing ledger state, no new schema. Sprint H2 (hardened machinery): fail-closed guards using the existing enforcement-gap vocabulary in packages/core/src/enforcement-gaps.ts. Sprint H3 (optimizations): call-count and race-window reduction. Related but separate: the lane worktree isolation plan (docs/architecture/LANE_WORKTREE_ISOLATION.md) ships independently; tasks here must not depend on lane machinery. Key files: apps/cli/src/commands.ts, apps/cli/src/command-registry.ts, packages/engine/src/runtime.ts, packages/core/src/enforcement-gaps.ts, packages/core/src/agent-directive-registry.ts, apps/mcp/src/tools.ts, tests/runtime/.
acceptanceCriteria: All three sprints closed with their tasks closed bottom-up, each task carrying command/test evidence and commit SHAs
bwrk doctor --strict --json passes after the final sprint merge
closedReason: Runtime hardening milestone completed and verified.
